question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` plus these token-budget helper exports as a stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold the token-count signal into the broader assemble metadata RFC?
rationale: The patch adds public plugin API surface that third-party context engines may compile against, while related assemble provenance/internal-event metadata is still under maintainer discussion.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Repairs
options.body: Approve the optional token-count API only after the message-count mismatch, generated artifacts, and real behavior proof are fixed.

options.title: Fold Into RFC Metadata Design
options.body: Pause this PR and land token counts together with the broader provenance/internal-event assemble metadata design tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82137.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Remove the SDK helper exports and limit this branch to internal wiring until a stable public helper shape is confirmed.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Repairs
recommendation.body: Approve the optional token-count API only after the message-count mismatch, generated artifacts, and real behavior proof are fixed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to this PR, authored the current branch head commits, and have the strongest recent history on the context-engine budget path.
